But the word of Jehovah was unto them,
Wherefore hear ye the word of Jehovah, ye scoffers;
Because ye have said: We have made a covenant with death,
Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah:
And I will set judgment for a line,
And your covenant with death shall be annulled;
As oft as it passeth through, shall it seize you;
For the bed is too short, for one to stretch himself out at length;
For as in mount Perazim, Jehovah will arise;
Now therefore give not up yourselves to scoffing,
Give ye ear, and hear my voice;
Doth the ploughman plough all day long that he may sow?
Doth he not also, when he hath levelled the surface thereof,
For He instructeth him as to the right way,
For the dill is not threshed with the threshing sledge,
Bread-corn is threshed:
This also cometh from Jehovah of hosts,
Wo to Ariel, to Ariel,
Yet I will bring distress upon Ariel;
And I will encamp against thee round about,
And thou shalt be brought low; and thou shalt speak out of the ground,
Moreover the multitude of thy strangers shall be like small dust,
From Jehovah of hosts cometh the visitation,
And like a dream, a night vision, shall be
It shall even be,
Stare ye now, and wonder!
For Jehovah hath poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep,
So that the whole vision is to you like the words of a sealed book,
And the book is delivered to one that knoweth not letters,
Wherefore the Lord hath said:
Therefore, behold, I will proceed to deal wonderfully
Wo unto them that seek with deep cunning to hide their counsel from Jehovah;
O your perverseness!
Is it not yet a very little while,
And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of this book;
The meek also shall increase their joy in Jehovah;
For the oppressor hath ceased, and the scoffer is no more;
They who would bring in a man guilty for a word,
Wherefore thus saith Jehovah to the house of Jacob,
For when his children shall see the work of my hands in the midst of themselves,
They also that have erred in spirit shall be full of understanding,
Wo unto the rebellious children, saith Jehovah,
Who set forward to go down to Egypt;
But the strength of Pharaoh shall be your shame;
When his princes were at Zoan,
They were all ashamed of a people that could not profit them;
THE ORACLE CONCERNING THE BEASTS OF THE SOUTH.
For Egypt shall help in vain, and to no purpose;
Now, go write it for them on a tablet;
For this is a rebellious people, lying children;
Who say to the seers, See not;
Get you out of the way,
Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel:
Therefore this iniquity shall be unto you
And it shall be broken, as the breaking of a potter's vessel that is broken in pieces;
Verily thus saith the Lord Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel:
And ye said: No, for we will flee upon horses;
One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one;
And therefore shall Jehovah delay, that he may be gracious unto you;
Surely the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem:
And the Lord shall give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction;
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee,
And ye shall defile the covering of your graven images of silver,
Then shall he give rain for thy seed,
And the oxen, and the young asses, that till the ground,
And there shall be upon every high mountain,
Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun,
Behold! the name of Jehovah cometh from afar,
And his breath is like an overflowing torrent,
Ye shall have a song, as in the night when the feast
And Jehovah shall cause his glorious voice to be heard,
When at the voice of Jehovah the Assyrian shall be beaten down,
And wherever the appointed rod shall pass,
For Tophet is ordained of old,
Wo unto them that go down to Egypt for help,
Yet He also is wise, and will bring evil;
Now the Egyptians are men, and not God;
For thus hath Jehovah said unto me:
As birds hover over their young,
Return unto him, from whom ye have deeply revolted,
Surely, in that day shall they cast away with contempt,
And the Assyrian shall fall by a sword not of man;
And for terror he shall pass by his strong hold,
Behold! a king shall reign in righteousness,
And a man shall be as an hiding-place from the wind,
And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim;
The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge,
The fool shall no longer be called honourable,
For the fool will still utter folly,
As for the fraudulent, his instruments are evil;
But the honourable man will devise honourable things,
Arise, hear my voice, ye women that are at ease,
Many days and years shall ye be disquieted, ye careless ones!
Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be disquieted, ye careless ones!
They lament for the fields,
Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers,
For the palace shall be deserted, the populous city shall be forsaken;
Until the Spirit be poured out upon us from on high;
Then judgment shall dwell in the wilderness,
And the work of righteousness shall be peace;
And my people shall dwell in a peaceful abode,
But it shall hail at the time when the forest is cut down,
Blessed are ye who sow your seed beside all waters,
Wo unto thee that spoilest, and thou hast not been spoiled;
O Jehovah, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee:
At the noise of the tumult the people fled;
But your spoil shall be gathered, as the caterpillar gathereth;
Jehovah is exalted, for he dwelleth on high:
And there shall be stability of thy times,
Behold their valiant men! they raise a cry without; The messengers of peace! they weep bitterly.
The highways are desolate,
The land mourneth, it languished!;
Now will I arise, saith Jehovah;
Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble;
And the people shall be as stones burnt into lime,
Hear, ye that are afar off, my doings;
The sinners in Zion are struck with dread,
He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly;
He shall dwell on high:
Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty:
Thine heart shall reflect on the terror:
That fierce people shalt thou see no more;
Look upon Zion, the city of our solemn feasts:
But there shall the Mighty One, Jehovah, be unto us
For Jehovah is our judge; Jehovah is our lawgiver;
Thy ropes are loosed, O thou enemy!
Neither shall the inhabitant say, I am sick:
Come near, ye nations, to hear;
For the indignation of Jehovah is upon all nations,
And their slain shall he cast out,
And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved.
For my sword hath already been made drunk in the heavens:
The sword of Jehovah is glutted with blood,
And with them shall be slaughtered the buffaloes,
For to Jehovah there is a day of vengeance,
And her streams shall be turned into pitch,
By night or by day it shall not be extinguished,
But the pelican and the porcupine shall possess it;
As for her nobles, there is not one there whom they might call to the government of the kingdom;
And in her palaces shall spring up thorns;
And the wild cats shall meet the jackals,
There shall the darting serpent make her nest, and lay her eggs:
Seek ye out of the book of Jehovah, and read:
And he hath cast the lot for them,
The desert, and the dry place, shall be glad for them;
It shall blossom abundantly,
Strengthen ye the feeble hands,
Say to the agitated in heart: Be strong,
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened,
Then shall the lame bound like the hart,
And the apparent water of the desert shall become a pool,
And an highway shall be there, even a road;
There shall not be a lion there,
And the ransomed of Jehovah shall return,
Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them.
And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the high-way of the fuller’s field.
Then came forth unto him Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.
And Rabshakeh said unto them: Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria: What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?
I say, sayest thou, (but they are vain words) there is counsel and strength for the war. Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?
Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; on which if a man lean, it will pierce his hand, and go through it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him.
But if thou say to me, We trust in Jehovah our God: is it not He, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and Jerusalem,

Ye shall worship before this altar? Now therefore give pledges, I pray thee, to my master the king of Assyria; and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.
How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master's servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
And am I now come up without Jehovah against this land to destroy it? Jehovah hath said unto me, Go up against this land and destroy it.

Then said Eliakim, and Shebna, and Joah, unto Rabshakeh: Speak, we beseech thee, to thy servants in the Syrian language, for we understand it; and speak not unto us in the Jewish language, in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.

But Rabshakeh said, Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? Hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own filth, and drink their own urine with you?
Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said: Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus saith the king: Let not Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you.
And let not Hezekiah make you trust in Jehovah; saying, Jehovah will certainly deliver us: this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.

Hearken not unto Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make peace with me and come out unto me. And eat ye every one of his own vine, and every one of his own fig-tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern;
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of corn and of wine, a land of bread and of vineyards.
Let not Hezekiah seduce you, saying, Jehovah will deliver us. Have the gods of the nations delivered, each his own land, from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? And have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their own lands out of my hand, that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
But they held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king's command was, saying, Answer him not.

Then came Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
And it came to pass when king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of Jehovah.
And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests covered with sackcloth, unto Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
And they said unto him: Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of distress, and of rebuke, and of contumely: for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth.

It may be that Jehovah, thy God, will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria hath sent to reproach the living God, and will reprove the words which Jehovah, thy God, hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is yet left.
And the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

And Isaiah said unto them: Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith Jehovah: Be not afraid because of the words which thou hast heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
Behold, I will bring a tremour upon him; and he shall hear a rumour, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.
So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyriah warring against Libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.
And he heard say concerning Tirhakah, king of Cush, He is come forth to make war with thee. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
Thus shall ye speak unto Hezekiah, king of Judah, saying Let not thy God, in whom thou trustest, deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all these lands by destroying them utterly; and shalt thou be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered those, whom my father have destroyed? as Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden which were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Henah, and of Ivah?
And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and he went up unto the house of Jehovah, and Hezekiah spread it before Jehovah.
And Hezekiah prayed unto Jehovah, saying:

O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, who dwellest between the Cherubims, Thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: Thou hast made the heavens, and the earth. Incline thine ear, O Jehovah, and hear;
open thine eyes, O Jehovah, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he hath sent to reproach the living God.
In truth, O Jehovah, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the nations, and their lands;
and have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them.
And now, O Jehovah, our God! save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Jehovah, even thou only.
Then Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sent unto Hezekiah, saying: Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel: Whereas thou hast prayed unto me, concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria:
This is the word which Jehovah hath spoken against him:
Whom hast thou reproached, and blasphemed;
By thy servants hast thou reproached the Lord, and hast said:
I have digged, and drunk water;
Hast thou not heard, that, from of old, I had disposed it?
Therefore were their inhabitants of small power,
But thy sitting down, and thy going out, and thy coming in, have I known;
Because thy rage against me, and thy insolence,
And this shall be a sign unto thee:
And the escaped of the house of Judah, which remain,
For from Jerusalem shall go forth the remnant,
Therefore thus saith Jehovah concerning the king of Assyria:
By the way through which he came, by the same shall he return;
And I will protect this city to deliver it,

Then an angel of Jehovah went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred and fourscore and five thousand men; and when man arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.
Then Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went, and returned; and dwelt at Nineveh.

And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat: and Esarhaddon, his son, reigned in his stead.

In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came unto him, and said unto him Thus saith Jehovah: Give charge concerning thine house: for thou shalt die and not live.
Then Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, mad prayed unto Jehovah.
And he said, Remember now, O Jehovah, I beseech thee, how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight And Hezekiah wept sore.
Then came the word of Jehovah to Isaiah, saying:
Go, and say unto Hezekiah, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of David thy father: I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: Behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years.
And I will deliver thee, and this city, out of the hand of the king of Assyria: and I will defend this city.
And this shall be a sign unto thee from Jehovah, that Jehovah will do this thing which he hath spoken.

Behold, I will cause the shadow of degrees, which hath gone down, by the sun, on the dial of Ahaz, to go back ten degrees. And the sun returned back ten degrees, by the degrees by which it had gone down.
THE WRITING OF HEZEKIAH KING OF JUDAH, WHEN HE HAD BEEN SICK, AND WAS RECOVERED FROM HIS SICKNESS.
I said: In the noontide of my days I shall go to the gates of the grave;
I said: I shall no more see Jehovah,
My habitation is taken down, and removed from me, like a shepherd's tent.
I resembled a roaring lion till the morning,
Like a swallow, or a crane, so did I twitter;
What shall I say?
O Lord, by these things do men live;
Behold, my bitter anguish is changed into health:
For the grave cannot praise thee,
The living, the living, he shall praise thee, as I do this day;
Jehovah was at hand to save me:
Now, Isaiah had said: Let them take a lump of figs, and lay it for a plaister upon the boil, and he shall
recover. Hezekiah also had said: What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of Jehovah?
At that time Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

And Hezekiah was glad of them, and shewed them his treasure-house, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found among his treasures. There was nothing in his house, or in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not shew them.

Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him: What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said: They came unto me from a far country, even from Babylon.
Then said he: What have they seen in thine house? And Hezekiah said: All that is in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures which I have not shewed them.
Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah:

Hear the word of Jehovah of hosts. Behold, the days shall come, when all that is in thine house, and all that thy fathers have treasured up unto this day, shall be carried away to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith Jehovah.
And of thy sons which shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: Good is the word of Jehovah, which thou hast spoken: He said, moreover, There shall be peace and truth in my days.
Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God:
Speak ye things pleasing to the heart of Jerusalem, and declare unto her,
A voice crieth in the wilderness,
Every valley shall be exalted,
And the glory of Jehovah shall be revealed,
A voice saith, Proclaim!
The grass withereth, the flower fadeth,
The grass withereth, the flower fadeth;
Get thee up upon a high mountain, O Zion, that bringest good tidings:
Behold, the Lord. Jehovah shall come with might,
He shall feed his flock, like a shepherd;
Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand,
Who hath searched out the Spirit of Jehovah,
With whom took he counsel, that he should instruct him;
Behold, the nations are as a drop from the bucket;
And Lebanon is not sufficient to supply fire,
All the nations are before him, as though they were nought;
To whom then will ye liken God?
The workman casteth an image,
He that is too poor to make a costly oblation chooseth him a piece of wood that will not rot;
Have ye not known? have ye not heard?
He it is who sitteth upon the circle of the earth,
Who reduceth princes to nothing;
Yea, they shall not scarcely be planted; yea, they shall not scarcely be sown;
To whom then will ye liken me?
Lift up your eyes on high,
Why sayest thou, O Jacob,
Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard,
He giveth power to the faint,
Even the youths shall faint and be weary,
But they that wait upon Jehovah shall gather new strength;
Keep silence before me, O Islands;
Who hath stirred up from the east him,
He hath pursued them, he hath passed safely,
Who hath wrought and done it,
The isles saw it, and feared;
They helped every one his neighbour,
So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith,
But thou, O Israel, my servant,
Thou, whom I have taken from the ends of the earth,
Fear not, for I am with thee;
Behold, all they that were enraged against thee shall be ashamed and confounded:
Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them, even the men that strove with thee:
For I Jehovah thy God, hold thee fast by thy right hand,
Fear not, thou worm Jacob; ye mortals of Israel;
Behold, I have made thee a new sharp threshing wain, armed with pointed teeth:
Thou shalt winnow them, and the wind shall carry them away,
The poor and needy who seek for water, and there is none;
I will open rivers in the high places,
I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia,
That they might see, and know,
Bring forward your cause, saith Jehovah:
Let them approach, and tell us the things that shall happen;
Tell us the things that will come to pass in the later times,
Lo, ye are worse than nothing;
I have raised up one from the north, and he shall come;
Who hath declared this from the beginning, that we should know it?
I am the first who said unto Zion, Behold, behold them I
And I looked, but there was no man;
Behold, they are all of them vanity;
Behold my servant, whom I will uphold;
He shall not cry, nor raise a clamour,
A bruised reed shall he not break,
He shall not despond, neither shall he be faint;
Thus saith the God, Jehovah,
I Jehovah have called thee in righteousness,
To open the blind eyes,
I am Jehovah, that is my name;
The former predictions, behold! they are come to pass;
Sing unto Jehovah a new song,
Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice,
Let them ascribe glory to Jehovah,
Jehovah shall march forth like a hero;
I have long time holden my peace,
I will make waste mountains and hills,
And I will lead the blind by a way that they knew not;
They are turned backward, they are utterly confounded,
Hear, ye deaf!
Who is blind, if not my servant?
Thou hast seen many things, but thou observest not;
Jehovah is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake;
But this is a people spoiled and plundered;
Who is there among you that will give ear to this?
Who hath given Jacob for a spoil,
Therefore he hath poured upon them the heat of his anger, and the vehemence of war:
But now, thus saith Jehovah that created thee, O Jacob,
When thou passest through the waters, I am with thee;
For I am Jehovah, thy God;
From the time that thou hast been precious in my sight,
Fear not, for I am with thee:
I will say to the north, Give up;
Even every one that is called by my name,
Bring forth the people that are blind, although they have eyes;
Let all the nations be gathered together,
Ye are my witnesses, saith Jehovah,
I, even I, am Jehovah;
I have declared my purpose, and I have saved;
Ever since time began I am He;
Thus saith Jehovah,
I am Jehovah, your Holy One;
Thus saith Jehovah,
Who hath brought forth the chariot and the horse, the army and the warrior;
Remember not the former things,
Behold, I make a new thing;
The wild beast of the field shall honour me,
This people whom I have formed for myself;
But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob!
Thou hast not brought me the lamb of thy burnt-offering,
Thou hast not bought for me with silver the sweet cane;
I, even I, am He,
Put me in remembrance; let us plead together:
Thy first father hath sinned,
Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary;
Yet now hear, O Jacob, my servant!
Thus saith Jehovah who made thee,
For I will pour waters upon the thirsty soil,
And they shall spring up as among the grass,
One shall say: I am Jehovah’s;
Thus saith Jehovah, the King of Israel,
And who like me could foretell,
Fear ye not, neither be afraid:
They that form a graven image are all of them vanity;
Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image,
Behold, all his associates shall be ashamed;
The smith maketh an axe,
The carpenter stretcheth out the line;
He heweth him down cedars,
Then shall it be for man to burn;
Part of it he burneth in the fire;
And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image:
They know not, neither do they understand;
Neither doth he consider in his heart;
He feedeth on ashes: a deluded heart leadeth him aside,
Remember these things, O Jacob,
I have blotted out as a thick cloud thy transgressions,
Sing, O ye heavens, for Jehovah hath done it;
Thus saith Jehovah, thy Redeemer,
I am He who frustrated the foretokens of the impostors,
Who established the word of his servant,
Who saith to the deep, Be dry;
Who saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd;
Thus saith Jehovah to his Anointed, to Cyrus,
I will go before thee,
And I will give thee the treasures of darkness,
For Jacob my servant’s sake,
I am Jehovah, and there is none else;
That men may know from the rising of the sun,
I form light, and create darkness;
Drop down, ye heavens, from above;
Wo unto him that striveth with his Maker!
Wo unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou?
Thus saith Jehovah,
I have made the earth,
I have raised him up in righteousness,
Thus saith Jehovah:
Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself;
They are ashamed, and also confounded, all of them;
But Israel shall be saved through Jehovah with an everlasting salvation:
For thus saith Jehovah who created the heavens;
I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth;
Assemble yourselves and come;
Publish it abroad, and bring them near; yea, let them take counsel together:
Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth:
I have sworn by myself, the truth is gone out of my mouth;
Only in Jehovah, shall one say of me, is righteousness and strength;
In Jehovah shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.
Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth;
They stoop, they bow down together:
Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob,
And even to your old age, I am the same;
To whom will ye liken me, and equal me?
They lavish gold out of the bag,
They bear him upon the shoulder; they carry him about;
Remember this, and shew yourselves men:
Remember the former things, of old time:
Declaring the end from the beginning,
Calling a ravenous bird from the east,
Hearken unto me, ye stubborn in heart,
I will bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off;
Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon I
Take the mill, and grind meal:
Thy nakedness shall be disclosed; yea, thy shame shall be seen:
Thus saith our Redeemer, Jehovah of hosts is his name,
Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans;
I was angry with my people, I polluted mine inheritance,
And thou saidst: I shall be a lady for ever:
Now, therefore, hear this, O thou voluptuous, that sittest in security:
Yet these two things shall come to thee in a moment,
But thou didst trust in thy wickedness, and saidst: None seeth me.
Therefore shall evil come upon thee,
Persist now in thine enchantments,
Thou art wearied in the multiplicity of thy counsels:
Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them up;
Thus will they prove to be unto thee, amongst whom thou hast laboured,
Hear this, O house of Jacob,
For they take their name from the Holy City,
The former events I declared of old;
Because I knew that thou wast obstinate,
Therefore I declared them to thee of old;
Thou hast heard; have now regard to the whole of it:
They are produced now, and not of old;
Yea, thou hast not heard; yea, thou hast not known;
For my name's sake I will defer mine anger;
Behold, I have purified thee in the fire, but not as silver;
For mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will I do it; for how should my name be profaned?
Hearken unto me, O Jacob,
Yea, my hand hath founded the earth,
Gather yourselves together all of you, and hear:
I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him:
Draw ye near unto me, and hear this:
Thus saith Jehovah,
O that thou hadst attended to my commandments!
